input.rationale: Section 1.4 is the operative grant in our favour: HDI provides the Company with access to and the right to use the hosting system and HDI's software and Content administration tools. It is not revocable at HDI's discretion (the only exit is the mutual 90-day termination right in Section 4.1), so it is not walk-away territory, and Section 10.3 already makes the Agreement inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by our successors and assigns, satisfying the fallback transfer element. However, the grant names only "the Company" and gives no path to add our affiliates, so it fails the fallback element requiring affiliate coverage on written notice. We therefore add one short sentence extending the Section 1.4 access and use rights to our affiliates on written notice, landing the clause at the fallback. Preferred features (contractors acting on our behalf, perpetual/irrevocable paid-up terms) are not pursued given the hosting-services nature of the grant.

proposal.summary: Extend the Section 1.4 access and use rights to the Company's affiliates on written notice to HDI.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the Section 1.4 access and use rights to our affiliates upon written notice to HDI, which is our fallback licence-scope position; Section 10.3 already carries these rights to our successors and assigns.

ops.text: The access and rights to use provided to the Company under this Section 1.4 shall extend to the Company's affiliates upon written notice to HDI.

mappings.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
